title: MLabs: Advancing Plutarch and CTL: CIP Integration, API Enhancements, and Improved Infrastructure

ms.promise:
・Extensions to the existing PByteString API to support CIP-122 and CIP-123 without unsafe builtin calls. This will be checked on the typelevel to ensure applications to builtin calls are always valid. 
・A new PBitString type with functions for CIP-122 and CIP-123 bit-oriented operations. 
・An API for CIP-121 conversion primitives involving PInteger, PByteString, and PBitString. Examples of new operations will be provided in the form of test cases. 
・Type class generalizations of the new operations with instances for PByteString and PBitString.
・Full test suite for compilation and semantic correctness for all functionalities, including property tests and compilation tests. The test suite will ensure said builtin functions we provide are correctly typed and have correct operation. We do not provide test cases for the operations themselves as they are already thoroughly tested by the plutus-core library. 
・API-level documentation and tutorials for all new types and functions. Haddock documentation will be auto-generated on each release and be published on the github pages.
ms.criteria:
・PByteString and PBitString support all of CIP-122 and CIP-123 operations safely and without builtin calls.
・CIP-121 conversion primitives work safely between PInteger, PByteString, and PBitString.
・Compilation and semantic tests validate these operations. 
・At least one type class generalization exists for PByteString and PBitString.
・Documentation is complete and explains usage, limitations, and invariants. Haddock documentation is published with new additional builtins.

ms.promise:
・Separate type classes for abstracting the predecessor and successor operation, with laws to ensure that these behave appropriately. PPosixTime must be a lawful instance of both of these.
・Support for negative PPosixTime values.
・Bugs regarding pcontains(issue #705). 
・Utility functions from plutarch-extra integrated into Plutarch which will reduce complexity of repository and setup. Required functions and utility types will be moved into the plutarch library itself.
・plutarch-orphanage separated into its own library. All the orphan instances, mainly instances for QuickCheck testing library, will be isolated into a single package for better code practice and easier upstreaming in the future.
・NoTracing option ensures elimination of all tracing code. By removing all traces, scripts can be further minimized without any script resources taken up by trace messages and pshow functions.
・Tests validating these enhancements.
ms.criteria:
・Behavior of pcontains is correct and is verifiable by regression tests and property tests.
・A type class for predecessor functionality, as well as laws describing the meaning of this functionality, exists.
・A type class for successor functionality, as well as laws describing the meaning of this functionality, exists.
・PPosixTime is a lawful instance of the type classes from 2 and 3.
・Negative PPosixTime is supported correctly with unit and property test cases. 
・plutarch-extra integrated, and plutarch-orphanage exists as a separate library.
・NoTracing removes all tracing code from Plutarch sc

ms.promise:
・Add SOP encoding to Plutarch, alongside Scott and Data encodings, and provide low-level operations for SOP encoding. UPLC version 1.1.0 introduced additional terms to encode Sum-of-Product at the UPLC term level. Since deconstruction of SOP terms can be done in one step, it yields better performance when compared to Scott and Data encoding.
・Enable multi-representation types (Scott, Data, SOP). The data representation system in the internal will be reworked to have more flexibility and approachable when supporting three representations–Scott, Data, SOP–at the same time.
・Tests to ensure that all three encodings (Scott, Data, SOP) work properly and that conversions between them are correct. Unit test cases and property based round-trip test cases will be provided to ensure decoding and encoding of each representation is behaving correctly.
ms.criteria:
・SOP encoding is integrated into Plutarch, with basic operations similar to PData. Test cases must be provided as a demonstration.
・Multi-representation types (Scott, Data, SOP) are fully supported, and conversions between them work seamlessly, demonstrated by a test suite.
・The PAsData infrastructure is reworked with the new multi-representation system to be more ergonomic and efficient for end users. Examples will be provided to demonstrate the changed interface.

ms.promise:
・Provide utilities for unrolling recursion and size optimization in Plutarch, using compile-time transformations that generate each step of recursion in order to reduce “start-up” costs relating to general recursion using fixed point combinator.
・Implement additional optimizations based on SOP support and representation conversion. This includes, but not limited to, application optimization using the `Case` term of UPLC.
・Ensure all functionalities for SOP support, conversions, and optimizations are thoroughly tested and documented. Golden test suites and benchmarks demonstrate improvements on execution units and script sizes.
・Include detailed comparisons of script sizes and execution costs before and after optimization to quantify the improvements.
・Update documentation website to provide examples and guides on the new features added.
ms.criteria:
・Optimization utilities for recursion unrolling and size optimization are functional, and their improvements are visible by numerical records generated by golden for regression test and performance benchmark .
・Additional optimizations based on SOP support and multi-representation are implemented and effective, and, again, their improvements are visible by numerical records generated by golden and benchmark.
・Additional features also provided test cases covering each use case for added features.
・The UPLC-benchmark repository is a Fund10 project ( https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/uplc-benchmark
ms.report:
:: UPDATES ::
--Reviewer 2
Thank you for raising this question. Our lead developer has investigated the increase in CPU and memory usage but did not identify any obvious missing optimizations or inefficiencies.
In the absence of a proper UPLC profiler, we can only offer an informed hypothesis. In Plutus V2, the datum and redeemer are passed as simple lambda arguments—effectively at no extra cost. In V3, however, they must be accessed via ScriptContext and ScriptInfo, which introduces additional overhead. Because this performance regression only appears in scripts that already consume very few execution units, we believe this change in datum/redeemer passing is the most likely culprit.

---
Please find our documentation links here:
https://plutarch-plutus.org/haddock/
https://plutarch-plutus.org/Introduction.html

・Create a PureScript package set that will include Cardano domain packages. Update CTL to use this package set, simplifying the upgrade process for clients. Make adjustments to the corresponding section in the documentation. 
・Create an NPM package containing all the necessary NPM dependencies required by CTL, eliminating the need for users to manually manage these dependencies with each CTL release. Update the relevant documentation section accordingly.
・Switch to HTTP interface for Ogmios. Currently, communication with Ogmios relies on WebSockets, which requires a dispatcher and adds unnecessary complexity. Transitioning to HTTP will allow us to reuse existing code, simplifying future maintenance.
